title: WhatsApp not bad
content:
WhatsApp’s not bad at all—it’s actually great for what it does. End-to-end encryption keeps your actual messages and calls private (no one, not even Meta, can read them), and it’s super reliable for texting, voice notes, video calls, groups, and sharing pics/videos across the world without paying extra. Works flawlessly on slow connections, syncs across devices, and the disappearing messages + status features make staying connected fun and easy. Love it for family chats, quick check-ins with friends abroad, and even some work stuff—simple, fast, no ads in chats.
But let’s be real: It’s owned by Meta (Facebook), so there are legit privacy dangers. They collect a ton of metadata (who you talk to, when, how often, your phone number, IP address, device info), and that gets shared within Meta for “improving services” or ads elsewhere. Backups aren’t encrypted by default (turn that on!), business chats can feed into Meta’s ecosystem, and features like Meta AI aren’t fully private. Scams/spam groups pop up too often, and if you’re super privacy-focused, it’s not Signal-level secure.
Still, for everyday use? It’s one of the best out there—billions trust it daily for a reason. Just stay aware, tweak your privacy settings (disable link previews, limit profile visibility, enable 2-step verification), and use it smart. 4.5 stars—love the app, cautious about the company.

title: Potential improvements
content: I love the app and it’s my main communication method. I just have some ideas that would make the app experience better. 1. It would be useful to have the possibility to filter (as you can do with unread messages) the group chats and individual chats. This would help to find chats easier. 2. The possibility to schedule messages to be sent at a certain time would be a major improvement. This would eliminate barriers created from different time zone as the app is used internationally. 3. Many of us use WhatsApp for everything including social and work related communication. And all chats and group chats are mixed together. It would be good to be able to add a label to chats according to a category. Then, you could filter the categories and find the ones that are under the label selected easily. This could be useful to save time and also to be able to prioritize messages. 4. Connected to the possibility to label chats to custom categories, it would be useful to put a schedule when you can receive messages in each label. Since most of us use the app as a work tool, but also as our main communication method. This creates a problem when trying to disconnect from work. It would be useful to pin chats (and group chats) to a category and be able to put certain schedule to when you can receive messages from each category of chats. This could help a lot to separate work from social life. This are just ideas that I would love to see through and hope the app continues to improve.

content: I just wanted to take a moment to express my appreciation for creating such a fantastic app. WhatsApp has truly revolutionized the way we connect with others, and I’m extremely impressed with the range of features it offers. But overall, WhatsApp has exceeded my expectations, and I look forward to its continued growth and improvements. Thank you for such a reliable and user-friendly app

title: Filled with scammers, not a secure app
content:
WhatsApp was what I used when I studied abroad to communicate with friends and family, but I unfortunately the app has so many issues that I refuse to use it even if that means it will be more difficult to communicate with those same friends and family living abroad. The app does provide some privacy in messaging, but based on the updated service agreements, it seems clear that Meta plans to use and train large language models on private messages. Additionally, WhatsApp has a series of issues regarding collecting metadata of its users and having nearly total freedom to monetize that information. I hate the idea of an app that claims to provide private and secure communication that is simultaneously monetizing my data.

The app is also filled with scammers. I receive near daily notifications from massive cryptocurrency scam groups adding me to group chats promising “massive returns on my investment.” No matter how many times I report these groups, they just keep popping up. I blame the extraction of all contacts from your phone that WhatsApp uses to help you communicate with others through the app. It’s clear that Meta is doing nothing to address these issues and they continue to violate our data while doing nothing.

If I could go back and never use the app in the first place, I would do it in a heartbeat. There other options for communication with family and friends abroad that does not come with the same issues that WhatsApp promises.

title: Absolutely horrible
content:
WhatsApp is an absolute disaster of an app, and Mark Zuckerberg should be ashamed of what he's turned it into. The platform is nothing more than a data-harvesting machine, stealing every ounce of personal information it can get its hands on. From your private messages to your contacts and location, nothing is sacred. The moment you install WhatsApp, you’ve essentially signed away your privacy, with WhatsApp profiting off your data in ways most people don’t even understand.

Let’s not forget that WhatsApp shares your data with advertisers and even other entities within Zuckerberg's empire, constantly bombarding you with targeted ads and influencing your every move. The so-called “privacy settings” are laughable at best—they are intentionally confusing and buried deep within layers of menus, ensuring that most users never have a chance to protect themselves. Zuckerberg and his team have built an empire on the backs of people’s privacy violations, all for the sake of profit. It's no wonder the app is riddled with security issues, invasive tracking, and personal data exploitation.

WhatsApp has become more about exploiting its users than providing any kind of meaningful communication. If you're still using WhatsApp, you're essentially handing over your life for free—while Zuckerberg and his company profit off of it. Do yourself a favor: delete your account and find a platform that values your privacy. WhatsApp is a data thief, plain and simple.

As I write this, it is only the begging of March, 2025. I should have at least 2 more months of time with which to migrate my use of WhatsApp to a newer, currently supported device. Instead, I am effectively locked out of the app, so I have no way of backing up my messages or transferring them. 

Please provide a fix for this. I have used WhatsApp happily for many years, and I would like to keep doing so.

title: Appreciation for Previous Fix & Persistent iOS UI Regression from Earlier Updates
content:
First of all, I would like to sincerely thank the WhatsApp team for fixing the issue I previously reported, where WhatsApp kept crashing on launch and I was unable to open or use the app on my iPhone. I really appreciate your effort in resolving that problem. WhatsApp is now opening and working normally.

I would also like to report another issue that has been present since some earlier WhatsApp updates and is still not resolved.

On my iPhone 16 Pro Max running iOS 26.0, the text input field inside chats is positioned too low and appears underneath the bottom navigation bar containing Calls, Chats, Updates, and Communities.

Because of this, the text field is difficult or sometimes impossible to access and use normally for typing messages.

This issue has been present for several previous versions of WhatsApp, so it does not appear to be related specifically to the latest update.

Please take a look at this issue and consider fixing the positioning of the chat text field so that it remains fully visible and accessible above the bottom navigation bar.

I would really appreciate it if this could be addressed in a future update.

Thank you again for fixing the previous crash issue and for your continued work on improving WhatsApp for iOS.

title: WhatsApp Keeps Crashing and Is Unusable
content:
I have been experiencing constant crashing issues with WhatsApp on my iPhone 13 Pro Max. The app opens normally but after a few seconds it suddenly closes, making it almost impossible for me to use WhatsApp at all.

I have already tried multiple troubleshooting methods, including restarting my iPhone, updating the app, uninstalling and reinstalling WhatsApp several times, and trying other recommended solutions, but the problem still continues.

I have also checked my iPhone Analytics Data and there are numerous WhatsApp crash reports, along with several JetsamEvent reports around the same period. This has been extremely frustrating because I have not been able to properly enjoy or use WhatsApp for days.

Please investigate this issue seriously and provide a permanent solution. I would really appreciate it if your technical team could look into why WhatsApp keeps crashing on my iPhone 13 Pro Max, because reinstalling the app repeatedly has not solved the problem.

I have important conversations and data on my WhatsApp, so I also need a solution that does not put my chats at risk.

Please help me resolve this issue as soon as possible. Thank you.

title: Important way to keep in touch for families
content: This app has been central in keeping my family connected. In my community, people often go to school and/or move to live all around the world. When my first daughter went to school in a different hemisphere than the rest of us, we all had to have different passcodes so as to be able to call each other without spending hundreds of dollars, sometimes for even one voice call. In the years before we found WhatsApp, I could only manage to get in touch with family members individually.  I certainly couldn’t keep contact day by day - there were too many of them, thank G-d. Now we not only have a family chat, we can have impromptu family video calls.  WhatsApp actually saved the life of one of my children, because they were too sick to even know how sick they were, much less call for help.  When a sibling discovered what was going on, my children ended up in the hospital for a few days.  I don’t have the time or space to describe the incredible asset WhatsApp has been for my family!

title: WhatsApp Privacy Features: Convenience or a Source of Confusion and Miscommunication?
content:
WhatsApp has become an essential communication tool, but some of its privacy features—like hiding online status and disabling read receipts—create more confusion than clarity. While these options are often marketed as privacy controls, they can easily lead to misunderstandings, overthinking, and unnecessary anxiety in conversations. When people cannot tell whether a message has been seen or whether someone is simply “offline,” it opens the door to misinterpretation and mental stress.
In many cases, these features don’t just protect privacy—they also enable avoidance and ambiguity in communication. If someone feels the need to hide their activity or responses from others, it raises the question of why they are connecting with those individuals in the first place. Honest and transparent communication should be the foundation of any interaction. If there is something to hide, perhaps it’s better not to engage with those people rather than creating an environment of uncertainty and confusion.
Ultimately, communication platforms should encourage clarity, not ambiguity. Features that obscure basic interaction signals may unintentionally harm trust and well-being rather than enhance user experience.

When people cannot tell whether a message has been seen or whether someone is simply “offline,” it opens the door to misinterpretation and mental stress.
In many cases, these features don’t just protect privacy—they also enable avoidance and ambiguity in communication. If someone feels the need to hide their activity or responses from others, it raises the question of why they are connecting with those individuals in the first place. Honest and transparent communication should be the foundation of any interaction. If there is something to hide, perhaps it’s better not to engage with those people rather than creating an environment of uncertainty and confusion.
Ultimately, communication platforms should encourage clarity, not ambiguity. Features that obscure basic interaction signals may unintentionally harm trust and well-being rather than enhance user experience.

title: Feature Proposal – “Temporary Group” Option for WhatsApp
content:
Dear WhatsApp Development Team,

I would like to propose the introduction of a “Temporary Group” feature to further enhance the user experience and simplify group management on WhatsApp.

Many users create short-term groups for events, projects, or specific occasions. Once the purpose of such groups is fulfilled, participants often hesitate to leave them manually. This hesitation is not only due to social courtesy but also because members may feel that exiting could appear discourteous or hurt the feelings of the group’s creator or admin. As a result, numerous inactive groups remain, leading to cluttered chat lists and reduced overall usability.

Proposed Feature:
When creating a group, WhatsApp could prompt the user to specify whether it is Temporary or Permanent.
If marked as Temporary, the following options could be offered:
•	Set an automatic deletion time (e.g., after 1 day, 1 week, or 1 month).
•	Send a reminder notification to all members prior to deletion.
•	Allow users to archive or export chat data before the group is deleted.

This feature would promote a more organized and comfortable communication environment, reduce social awkwardness, and reflect WhatsApp’s continued commitment to user-friendly innovation. It addresses both emotional and practical aspects of group interactions while keeping the platform clean and efficient.

Thank you for considering this suggestion. I believe such an enhancement would be widely appreciated by users worldwide.

Kind regards,
WhatsApp User

title: Annoyingly Weak Messenger
content:
Compared to other free messaging apps, this may be the most boring and even irritating one available. Here are just some of the problems I had with this piece of under-deveolped garbage:
1. There’s a very limited time during which you can delete your messages for the other party after you send them. I can’t even see why this option should not be always available.
2. Even if you’re luck and do get the chance to delete your sent message, Whatsapp still informs the receiving party that you have deleted your message! If I‘d wanted him/her to know this, I wouldn’t delete my message in the first place!
3. Old messages go out of reach after some time and there comes a stupid pop-up that says “request the other participant in this chat to send the message again!” Why?! Obviously in many cases this would be a ridiculous thing to ask.
4. Voice messages are so troublesome. As an example, you cannot play them with a faster/slower speed or while you’re in another chat. And there are a lot of other stupid problems with music/voice files.
5. Working with other file formats can get even more frustrating. It seems that the developers had only one function in mind: sending and receiving plain text messages and nothing more.
6. You virtually can’t have access to the app only via your PC or laptop. There is a Web version but it required you to stay connected with the app on your phone! It’s really ridiculous.
7. You cannot use this crappy app on any other device. You’re limited to just one phone at a time.

title: My Account was hacked and WhatsApp is unable to help
content:
I’ve found WhatsApp to be increasingly unreliable, especially when it comes to account security and customer support. My account was compromised last year, and despite reaching out to WhatsApp multiple times, all I’ve received are automated emails with no real solutions or follow-up. No one ever personally contacted me to assist in recovering my account.

What’s most concerning is how easy it seems for hackers to gain access to your account, contact list, and any other information linked to your WhatsApp. This app appears to be set up in a way that leaves users extremely vulnerable, giving unscrupulous individuals the ability to take over accounts without any meaningful way to trace or stop them.

Unlike other platforms such as Facebook, which offer more visible layers of protection and recovery options, WhatsApp seems to lack both accountability and a reliable security infrastructure. Until they make serious improvements, I strongly caution anyone considering downloading or using this app. It simply doesn’t feel safe, and it seems like WhatsApp doesn’t care enough to protect its users.

title: Appalling Experience! Arbitrary Number Suspension by WhatsApp!
content:

The timing of WhatsApp's arbitrary number suspension couldn't have been more disastrous, leaving me in a state of extreme distress with no means of reaching the hotel.

author: Van Oie

title: Not so excellent
content:
WhatsApp has been one of the most reliable messaging apps for years. The interface is simple, clean, and easy to use, making it accessible for all types of users. Features like voice and video calls, group chats, and file sharing work smoothly most of the time, and end-to-end encryption adds a strong sense of privacy and security.

However, there are still some areas that need improvement. Backup and restore processes, especially when switching devices, can be frustrating and time-consuming. The app also tends to consume a lot of storage due to media files, and managing that isn’t always convenient. Occasionally, there are bugs or delays in notifications as well.

Overall, WhatsApp is still a must-have app for communication, but with a few updates and optimizations, it could be significantly better.

title: Selective Communication Disconnection
content:
I would like to suggest introducing a new feature that allows users to temporarily disconnect communication with specific contacts, without using the traditional block option. This feature would function similarly to disabling internet access for selected individuals.

The idea is to let WhatsApp remain active and functional while making the user appear offline or unreachable to certain contacts. This would be particularly useful in situations where users want to avoid communication from specific numbers without resorting to blocking them, which may feel too permanent or socially sensitive.

Such a feature would enhance user control and privacy, offering a more flexible and less intrusive alternative to blocking.

title: "Start chatting”
content:
The addition of the "Start chatting" suggestions is one of the worst interface decisions WhatsApp has made. It clutters the Chats screen with contacts I did not ask to see and cannot permanently remove. There is no option to disable this feature, forcing it on every user regardless of preference.
Beyond being unnecessary, these suggestions can create privacy and social issues by repeatedly surfacing contacts that users may not want displayed. The feature adds no value for those of us who use WhatsApp daily and simply makes the app feel more intrusive and less organized.
Good design gives users control. If someone wants contact suggestions, let them enable them. If they don't, they should be able to turn them off. Removing user choice is a step backward.
Please stop forcing unwanted features into the app and add a simple toggle to permanently hide the "Start chatting" section. Until then, the experience remains significantly worse than it was before this update.

title: UPDATES
content:
I am leaving a 1-star review due to my frustration with WhatsApp’s forced update policy. I am perfectly content with the version I currently have, but I am being pressured to update. These updates do not improve the app—in fact, they often make the experience worse.

Every time I open the app, I am prompted to update, and when I select the “Learn More” link to understand why updates are mandatory, the app immediately crashes and returns me to my home screen. This issue has persisted to the point where now, when I open WhatsApp, I only see a black screen. I am unable to use the app at all simply because I chose not to update.

As a loyal user, I should have the option to decide whether I want to update the app, especially when the updates fail to enhance functionality or add value. Forcing users into updates and then penalizing them for noncompliance—by essentially locking them out of the app—is unacceptable. I strongly urge WhatsApp to reconsider this policy and respect users’ autonomy

title: Inconsistent. But overall love WhatsApp.
content:
I absolutely love WhatsApp. I have to say it’s by far my most favorite messaging app. It has features that even iPhone/Apple hasn’t figured out yet, like: being on a video call and another call that calls through on your phone, you can answer without it hanging up the WhatsApp video call. Apple has NOT mastered this with FaceTime 🤦‍♀️. As well, WhatsApp just offers a lot of options for privacy and security and the end to end encryption will always be a win for me.

My only real complaint is that there have been times I have tried to find certain settings on WhatsApp when trying to turn off a toggle or lock something, and when the instructions say something like “turn off media visibility”, and I follow the step by step instructions to do so, that option isn’t available in my WhatsApp. Just like for a while there, I was unable to access the settings button in my Locked Chats, even, the options literally wasn’t even visible. WhatsApp doesn’t have any real type of chat support that actually helps you with resolutions, so it can be quite frustrating.

WhatsApp should have an easier way to turn off the option to “not save pics/media that are taken by ME in the app, to my camera roll”. They have it so you don’t have to autosave from people who send media to you, but they need to do it for outgoing media as well.

So recap:
1. Needs to make all settings options available to ALL WhatsApp users.
2. Needs to have an option not to autosave outgoing media to phone/camera roll.
3. GET BETTER TECH SUPPORT!!! Please!

Otherwise, the app is absolutely amazing!

title: whatsapp stickers
content:
Dear WhatsApp Support Team,

I would like to raise a concern regarding the use of personal photos to create stickers on WhatsApp.

It has become increasingly common for users to take photos of other people, turn those photos into WhatsApp stickers, and share them in group chats. Even when this is initially done as a joke or without harmful intentions, these stickers can easily be saved, forwarded, and circulated beyond the original group without the person’s knowledge or consent.

This can cause embarrassment, discomfort, and privacy concerns, especially because once a sticker begins circulating, the person shown in it has very little control over where it may be shared or how it may be used.

I kindly ask WhatsApp to consider additional privacy and safety measures regarding stickers created from identifiable personal photos. For example, there could be an easier way for individuals to report stickers containing their image or request restrictions on their further distribution.

I believe addressing this issue would help protect users’ privacy and reduce the misuse of personal images on the platform.

Thank you for taking this concern into consideration.

Kind regards

content:

After using a cleaner to rid my phone of the junk, and my camera works again, that’s when a certain person who wanted to chat some time ago suddenly says hi again, and my camera stops working again. Repeating the cleansing, then trying to open WhatsApp to delete the conversation resulted in WhatsApp crashing two or three times, then my WhatsApp screen went black. Then another cleaning  and WhatsApp crashing several times until I deleted WhatsApp.
Now my phone functions normally, including the camera.

WhatsApp is NOT secure anymore.
Understand that hackers see the public as a source of unlimited funds - it’s only a matter of continuing to attempt accessing everything.

title: Needs upgrading
content:
I believe this app needs some reformation. Let’s say someone who you don’t want to contact you anymore continues to keep calling you? Okay now you block them they could create a new account and since you can’t change your number unless you get a new number they can literally keep calling you… make usernames available for Whatsapp or something!! Also whenever you delete an account your number should disappear as well not stay there!! I will never be giving my number out via this app again.

Reformation steps I recommend:

Stronger Blocking Mechanism: Ensure that when you block someone, it’s more comprehensive. For instance, prevent blocked users from contacting you through newly created accounts or any secondary numbers they might add.
2.	Enhanced Privacy Options: Give users more control over their visibility. For example, allowing users to hide their phone numbers entirely from non-contacts or people outside their chosen groups.
3.	Account Deletion Process: When an account is deleted, the associated phone number should be immediately removed from WhatsApp’s database, ensuring that the deleted number cannot be contacted through WhatsApp again.
4. Temporary Disabling of Accounts: Allow users to temporarily disable their account without needing to change their phone number, making it harder for stalkers or unwanted contacts to reach them.
5.	Multiple Blocking Levels: Introduce more specific block settings, such as blocking someone from only calling you or messaging you, depending on what boundaries you want to set. For example: the number of calls someone can send you if you’re clearly not responding to them.

title: Status Duration.
content:
WhatsApp team,
For the most part, the app has been effective in keeping touch with friends and family, but there is always room for improvement.
Currently, users can only pin statuses for 24 hours, which can be limiting for those who want to share important updates that may need to stay up for longer periods of time. I think it would be helpful if users are allowed to choose how long they prefer a single or multiple shared status to stay pinned on duration, whether that's 24 hours, 48 hours, or even longer.
Overall, extending the duration for pinned statuses on WhatsApp would enhance the user experience and provide more customization options for individuals to curate their profiles and share important information with their contacts. Hope this is deliberated on and implemented asap.🙂
Thanks.

title: WARNING: You HAVE to use your real number
content: Read ahead for those with kids: To sign up for WhatsApp, you have to share your real phone number. This is forced because on sign up they uses carrier pinging through 2FA to ensure you’re using your real number and not a burner. And that’s just where it starts. Now, the only way to have others contact you is with your real number. All your contacts see your real number, any one you chat to can see your real number. This is dangerous because even if you block and unsavory chat, that person still has your actual number. If that person is blocked on the app, they can still call, text, and harass whomever is on the other line. I immediately had my family delete their accounts and private data from Facebook/WhatsApp. If you value your families privacy or your own, here’s my recommendations for apps that do actually care about user privacy: Signal, Telegram, Wire Do better Facebook.

title: Random Number Suspension Following Trip to Europe
content:
I have heard that this could happen… and now it has. I see that I’m not the only person it has happened to, as well.

Thus, I messaged with them to coordinate getting them to our hotel in Thessaloniki. Thank goodness, WhatsApp actually functioned in that moment, because their hotel was terrible! They needed to get to our hotel and get a different room.

Unfortunately, however, I just popped WhatsApp open so that I could message someone in Italy to schedule a highly anticipated consultation with two world renowned voice teachers… only to find WhatsApp has banned my number! They are awaiting my message, and I can’t message them! I’m incredibly disappointed and can do nothing but submit my request for review (which said nothing other than, “I’m confused,” because I didn’t remember in my upset that this was a thing until after I submitted the review) and submit this review here and beg for help.

Shame on WhatsApp for not fixing this problem!!! They pride themselves on being THE solution for international communication, but this is what happens?! What kind of solution is this supposed to be?!

title: Frustrating and Outdated
content:
WhatsApp has so much potential, but it’s riddled with issues that make it a frustrating platform to use.
1.	Lack of Privacy: Despite claims of end-to-end encryption, being owned by Meta raises serious concerns about how user data is handled. The connection between WhatsApp, Facebook, and Instagram feels intrusive.
2.	Frequent Glitches: Messages sometimes fail to send or receive, group chats get stuck loading, and notifications don’t always show up properly. Basic reliability is an issue.
3.	Limited Customization: The app’s customization options for themes, notifications, and layouts are far behind competitors like Telegram. It feels dated.
4.	Slow Feature Rollouts: Features like multi-device support and improved file sharing were introduced far too late and still don’t work seamlessly.
5.	Poor Moderation: Spam and scam messages are rampant, and there’s no effective system to block or filter them. Reporting these accounts seems pointless.
6.	No Cross-Device Syncing: You still can’t easily switch between devices without a hassle. Messages aren’t stored in the cloud, which feels archaic in 2025.
7.	Customer Support is Nonexistent: If you encounter an issue, good luck finding any meaningful support. The FAQs don’t address nuanced problems, and there’s no way to contact a real person.
8.	Updates Ruin the App: New updates often introduce more bugs than improvements. The app feels poorly tested before rolling out changes.

WhatsApp is no longer the gold standard for messaging. Its outdated interface and constant frustrations make it hard to recommend over alternatives like Signal or Telegram.

title: Disappointed
content:
WhatsApp used to be my go-to messaging app, but over time, it has become increasingly unreliable and frustrating. One of the biggest issues is the constant syncing problems—sometimes messages just don’t come through, and you have to manually refresh or restart the app. The notifications are often delayed, and I’ve missed important messages because of it.

The app also feels bloated with unnecessary features like status updates, which I never use, but seem to take up space in the interface. The lack of customization options is another drawback—you're stuck with a generic chat layout and minimal control over how the app looks or works.

The privacy concerns have also grown significantly. The integration with Facebook (now Meta) feels like a major step backward, and it's unclear how much of your data is being shared or tracked across platforms. It’s hard to trust an app that constantly seems to prioritize corporate interests over user privacy.

Additionally, video and voice calls often suffer from poor quality, especially on weaker connections, and it’s still prone to crashing or freezing, making basic functions unreliable. Overall, it’s disappointing how an app that was once simple and effective has now become bogged down with bugs, ads, and questionable privacy practices.

title: WhatsApp is No Longer Secure Communication
content:
When I first started using WhatsApp, it was a straightforward, secure, and ad-free way to communicate with friends and family around the world. The focus was on privacy and simplicity—everything you’d want in a messaging app. But since Meta took over, the experience has steadily declined.

The app now feels less about connection and more about monetization. Meta’s creeping data practices, combined with their attempts to push features like business accounts and integrations, have made WhatsApp feel less private and more like another way for Meta to profit off its users. Even with claims of end-to-end encryption, it’s hard to trust a company that has consistently prioritized engagement and profit over transparency.

Like Facebook and Instagram, WhatsApp is now tied to Meta’s broader ecosystem of divisive politics and misinformation. The platform has also become a breeding ground for fake news, amplified by Zuckerberg’s recent decision to stop fact-checking certain types of content. It’s troubling to see a platform once known for secure and simple communication become another channel for unchecked propaganda and poorly targeted ads.

WhatsApp used to be a reliable and trusted messaging app. Now, it’s just another cog in Meta’s machine, and it’s no longer worth using if you value your privacy and sanity. Disappointing.

The platform has also become a breeding ground for fake news, amplified by Zuckerberg’s recent decision to stop fact-checking certain types of content. It’s troubling to see a platform once known for secure and simple communication become another channel for unchecked propaganda and poorly targeted ads.

WhatsApp used to be a reliable and trusted messaging app. Now, it’s just another cog in Meta’s machine, and it’s no longer worth using if you value your privacy and sanity. Disappointing.

title: Great app, but needs MORE privacy options
content:
The Read Receipts and the Last Seen are very LIMITED in their options.

Here are a couple of features I wish to see in WhatsApp:

LAST SEEN:
- Exceptions: in addition to the original options (Everyone, My Contacts, Nobody), *Exceptions* gives you the option to include or exclude specific contacts from the above settings.
(Telegram app already has this! I don’t know why WhatsApp hasn’t!)

READ RECEIPTS:
- option to turn on/off *read receipts* for INDIVIDUAL contacts. (iMessage already has this option!)

Or similar to the Last Seen options (in telegram):
- “Enable Read Receipts” for: Everyone, My Contacts, Nobody,” with Exceptions!

The purpose of the additional options is:

We all have a variety of contacts. From those who bombard you with messages when they see you were recently online (and/or text you as soon as they see the Read Receipt) to your friends who are more respectful of your space.

We have some contacts from whom we’d rather have more privacy; while others with whom we’d like to have more transparency. With EXCEPTIONS option, you can say goodbye to the “tossing-the-baby-with-the-bath-water” problem.

title: From Secure Messaging to Meta’s Data Playground
content:
WhatsApp was once the gold standard for secure messaging, but ever since Meta took over, it’s been sliding downhill. Despite its claims of being privacy-focused, there are plenty of reasons to be skeptical:

1.	Metadata Collection: Sure, messages are end-to-end encrypted, but WhatsApp collects an absurd amount of metadata—who you contact, how often, when, and where. All of this is handed over to Meta to fuel their ad empire.

2.	Controversial Privacy Policy (2021): Meta tried forcing users to share data with Facebook or lose access to the app. The backlash was loud, but it showed where their priorities lie: profits over privacy.

3.	Global Outages: Meta’s repeated server issues leave users stranded, with WhatsApp going down globally at least once a year. A messaging app this big should be more reliable.

4.	Group Data Leaks: WhatsApp group invite links have repeatedly shown up on Google searches, exposing private group chats to anyone.

5.	Weak Backup Security: Chat backups stored on Google Drive or iCloud are not end-to-end encrypted by default, leaving them vulnerable to breaches.

Beyond privacy, the app feels stagnant. Features roll out at a snail’s pace, and many of them (like disappearing messages) are half-baked or copied from other apps. Meanwhile, competitors like Signal and Telegram are miles ahead in both functionality and respect for user privacy.

WhatsApp is a shadow of what it used to be. If you care about truly secure communication and want to avoid feeding Meta’s endless appetite for data, it’s time to switch to a more trustworthy alternative.

title: Is privacy a concern of yours?
content:
It used to be about a year ago that I could use this app without giving them access to my contacts. Then they changed that. And recently expanded it to this (copied from Apple’s privacy statement about this app):

The following data may be collected and linked to your identity:

Purchases, Financial Info, Location, Contacts, Contact Info, Identifiers, User Content, Diagnostics, Usage Data

I don’t know about you, but I’m very leary about an app potentially collecting my purchases, financial info, all my conversations (Content), and selling my info for their, and 3rd party, marketing, etc. Even if the company vehemently denies they don’t do this, I don’t trust a “free” service to NOT sell your info. They need to make money somehow. And how do I know how else they may be using my data? Read their own huge privacy statement and judge for yourself how vague it is.

If you are not concerned, then go ahead and use it. When it first started, it was a great app. I used it all the time. Since I no longer use it since the change, I can’t tell you how good (or bad) the app has become. And yes, I know millions use it all the time. Almost everyone I know does. I just don’t like invasive apps like this. This has a long and scary privacy list compared to many other apps.

title: 0/5 going downhill
content:
WhatsApp has become a disappointing app with several issues:
1.Privacy Concerns: While it claims to have end-to-end encryption, its parent company, Meta, has a questionable history with user data. The privacy policy changes have left users feeling uneasy about how their data is handled.
2.Intrusive Updates: The app often pushes unnecessary features like Status updates, which feel like a poor imitation of Instagram Stories. It’s a messaging app—stop overcomplicating it!
3.No Multi-Device Independence: While you can use WhatsApp on multiple devices, it still relies heavily on a phone connection for many features, making it inconvenient.
4.Unreliable Notifications: Messages and notifications are often delayed, especially after updates, making it unreliable for important communications.
5.Lack of Customization: There are minimal options for customizing themes or chat layouts, leaving the app feeling outdated and bland.
6.Storage Hog: Media files are saved automatically, taking up excessive space on devices. Managing this manually is frustrating and time-consuming.
7.No Real Customer Support: There’s no effective way to resolve issues. The app relies on automated responses, leaving users without real help.
8.Spam and Scams: Despite encryption, WhatsApp is full of spam messages and scams. The platform doesn’t do enough to filter out bad actors.
9.Group Chat Limitations: Features like large group chats and broadcast lists are clunky and lack advanced moderation tools.

Overall, WhatsApp is no longer the simple, efficient messaging app it once was. It feels bloated, unreliable, and increasingly focused on monetization rather than user experience. Highly disappointing.

title: WhatsApp’s File Sharing Is Stuck in the Stone Age
content:
WhatsApp may still rule the messaging world, but its media features are a disaster. Video and file sharing? Practically useless. The app crushes video quality so hard your videos end up looking like they were recorded on a potato. Want to send a high-quality file? Forget it—size limits and compression turn everything into pixelated garbage.

And don’t even think about switching apps while something uploads. If you’re not actively staring at the screen, uploads stall or fail completely—with zero warning. You might think a video sent, but nope—WhatsApp just gives up silently. In 2025, how is this still a thing?

To make matters worse, they’ve now removed one of the most basic features: seeing if your voice messages were listened to. Why? Nobody knows. But it’s yet another example of WhatsApp quietly stripping away useful functionality for no apparent reason.

WhatsApp isn’t just stagnant—it’s regressing. Meta has the tech and the money to do better, but right now, this app is a clunky, unreliable shadow of what it could be. Fix media sharing. Fix background uploads. Bring back voice message read indicators. Right now, WhatsApp is a messaging app that flops the moment you try to do anything more than type “hi.”

Adding both local storage and iCloud backup options would greatly improve the user experience.

title: No meaningful support
content:
I rely on WhatsApp every day in my role coordinating hundreds of people. Until recently, I considered it an excellent platform. Unfortunately, my recent experience has made it impossible to trust for mission-critical communication.

My account has now been repeatedly restricted by WhatsApp’s automated systems. After each review, my account is restored, but then it is restricted again immediately—even after sending a single normal message to a single contact. This was not a broadcast, not automation, and not spam.

The most frustrating part is the complete lack of meaningful customer support. Every attempt to seek help results in automated AI responses with no way to reach a human being who can investigate what appears to be an obvious error.

I understand the need to fight spam, but when legitimate users can be repeatedly locked out without explanation or an effective appeal process, the platform becomes unreliable for anyone who depends on it for important communication.

WhatsApp has become a single point of failure for my organization, and because there is no realistic way to resolve an incorrect restriction, I am now evaluating alternative communication platforms. I hope Meta invests in providing genuine human support for cases where its automated systems make mistakes.

title: From Communication to Data Exploitation
content:
WhatsApp used to be the gold standard of messaging apps—simple, reliable, and private. But then Meta got its grimy, greed-ridden hands on it, and now it’s just another cog in Zuckerberg’s surveillance machine. The app’s tagline should be: “Free Messaging… But Your Privacy Costs Extra!”

End-to-end encryption? Sure, they market it like they care about privacy, but let’s not forget who’s running the show. Meta’s whole business model revolves around harvesting your data and turning it into cold, hard cash. You really think they’re not mining everything they can from your metadata? WhatsApp is basically Zuckerberg’s trojan horse into your personal life, pretending to care about privacy while selling you out on the back end.

And let’s talk about the app itself: constant glitches, unnecessary updates, and an endless push for useless features nobody asked for. Communities? Channels? Who cares? WhatsApp isn’t innovating—they’re throwing spaghetti at the wall, hoping something sticks while their actual competitors blow them out of the water.

If you’re looking for an alternative, check out Signal or Telegram. They’re faster, more reliable, and actually care about privacy. WhatsApp? It’s just a surveillance tool with a chat feature slapped on top.

I would really appreciate it if you took this concept into consideration.

title: Meta Prioritizes Greed Over Users’ Interests
content:

The company continues to prioritize profit over genuine connection, and its role in pushing for bans like TikTok highlights just how far they’re willing to go to crush competition. Instead of innovating or improving their platforms, Meta seems focused on monopolizing the social media landscape at the expense of user choice and freedom.

The relentless push for ad revenue, invasive data practices, and now involvement in lobbying against competitors prove that the company is more concerned about its billionaire owners’ wallets than about fostering meaningful online communities. It’s disheartening to see such a large platform lose sight of its purpose.

If you’re tired of supporting greed-driven tech giants, look elsewhere. There are better platforms out there that actually care about their users. Meta is not one of them.

title: WhatsCrap: A Gorified Group Chat Nightmare
content:
⭐☆☆☆☆

WhatsApp is the tech equivalent of that one friend who only shows up when they need something—usually your attention or your phone storage. Sure, it claims to be “secure” and “simple,” but in reality, it’s a chaos machine designed to ruin your peace of mind, one unwanted group chat at a time.

First off, let’s talk about the notifications. This app is basically a digital toddler, constantly screaming for attention. Missed a message? Prepare for 27 reminders that someone from your family group chat shared another blurry photo of their lunch. And don’t even think about muting chats—it’s like muting a fire alarm that just keeps going off.

And the group chats? Absolute madness. You join one for a work project, and next thing you know, you’re stuck in a 50-person thread where half the people are sending “Good morning ☀️” gifs, and the other half are forwarding conspiracy theories from 2013. There’s no escape. If you leave the chat, everyone notices, and then you’re “that guy.”

Also, why is every family member over 50 obsessed with sending chain messages about how Mark Zuckerberg is spying on us via WhatsApp? Newsflash, Aunt Carol: he’s too busy ruining Instagram. Meanwhile, the app still feels like it’s running on technology from the Stone Age. Customization? Nope. Basic organization? Forget it. It’s a digital jungle where your messages go to get lost forever.

In conclusion: WhatsApp is less of a messaging app and more of a social burden. Between the relentless spam, endless drama, and constant updates that fix nothing, it’s like a toxic relationship you can’t quite quit. Do yourself a favor—ditch it, and go back to carrier pigeons. They’re quieter and less invasive.

title: Wish my boyfriend would get an iPhone
content: My (super) long distance man and I use this every day as our normal text/call/“facetime” app. We use the video and audio call functions quite often, but I’ve found that the audio is not very good. Background noises are extremely loud (sheets rubbing against the phone, outside rain or sirens, sounds of doors opening/closing, etc.), while the voice of the person speaking is many times intelligible. When the call is “reconnecting”, we are always forced to hang up, as the beeping sound is completely unbearable. It does it’s job, and is a very useful app for people without iPhones or people from different countries. Just wish the audio quality was nicer and the beeping would be at least slightly less obnoxious.

This would be similar to the “Message Request” feature already available in WhatsApp for people not saved in the contact list, but with the added functionality of notifying the user when they receive a message from someone they haven’t interacted with before.

This feature would allow users to have better control over unsolicited messages and ensure privacy while still giving the opportunity to engage with new contacts if desired. It would be a great addition for users who prefer a cleaner and more organized messaging experience.

Thank you for considering this suggestion. I look forward to seeing WhatsApp continue to improve and innovate.

Best regards,
Haris Rohesh

title: Unfair WhatsApp Account Restriction Due to Unsolicited Group Additions
content:
I am extremely disappointed with the way WhatsApp handles account restrictions and reviews. My account was placed under review, leaving me without access to an important means of communication, even though the situation appears to have been caused by problems within WhatsApp’s own system.

WhatsApp allows people to add users to groups they never requested or wanted to join. A user should not be penalized or lose access to their account because other people add their number to unsolicited groups or because automated systems incorrectly interpret that activity as suspicious.

It is unfair to leave a legitimate user without communication while the account is being reviewed, especially when the user has little or no control over the activity that triggered the restriction.

WhatsApp should improve its automated detection and review process so that legitimate users are not punished for unsolicited group activity. There should also be a faster and more transparent way to resolve these situations.

I hope WhatsApp reviews my case fairly, restores my account promptly, and improves its system to prevent this from happening to other users.

title: Privacy Claims Are Misleading
content:
WhatsApp markets itself as a “secure” platform with end-to-end encryption, but don’t be fooled—it’s owned by Meta, the same company infamous for privacy violations and data exploitation. While your messages may be encrypted, the app collects a shocking amount of metadata: who you talk to, when, how often, and even your location if enabled. This information is shared with Meta to fuel their advertising empire.

Worse, WhatsApp’s policies and updates have consistently eroded user trust, with vague terms and a lack of transparency about how your data is used. Recent breaches and questionable data-sharing practices make it clear that WhatsApp isn’t the safe, private messaging app it claims to be.

If you value your digital privacy, it’s time to switch to a more trustworthy platform. WhatsApp is nothing but a wolf in sheep’s clothing.

In conclusion, while the product itself is useful, the customer service experience is very poor and does not meet the global importance of the application.
